newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bangkok subway contract for $944 mln signed.
newsitem.headline: Bangkok subway contract for $944 mln signed.

text.p: The Thai government and representatives of the BCKT consortium signed a US$944 million contract to build the initial phase of Bangkok's first subway system on Tuesday.

"I think it is a moment of history," said Theerapong Attajarusit, Managing Director of the Metropolitan Rapid Transit Authority, which evaluated the bids for this first 11 km of a the proposed 22 Km system.

The consortium members, Gemany's Bilfinger + Berger, Thailand's Ch Karnchang and Japanese firms Tokyu Construction and Kumagai Gumi said work will be shared equitably, but said revenue and work sharing details have not been finalised.
"This is a joint venture and we will share responsibilities, totally," said Harmut Tolle managing director of Bilfinger + Berger Asia.
But he said the fact they already had Bilfinger + Berger tunnelling equipment in Taiwan was a consideration that should be made when the parties decided on who should perform the tunnelling.
Tolle said construction of cut and covered stations for the project would start early next year. Tunnelling was expected to begin within one to two year.

A tender, worth over 20 billion baht, for the second 11 km northern phase of the line, is now open with BCKT widely expected to win this contract too. The initial technical evaluation of the five bids received is expected to take six weeks.
A tender contract for a further 11 billion baht concession for fittings and track for the entire length of the project is expected to be awarded within the next two years.
